{"self_assessment": "Impact: My role was the joins. I curved a few dominoes round the nose to link the end of the top line into the start of the bottom line, which let the fall travel from the start all the way round the fish outline. That joint was the one place the two halves of the picture had to meet, so it mattered to the result. The fish is built, and by my inspection the fall carries through nearly all of the standing dominoes, both tail tips included.

Execution: I laid a small stretch of dominoes at the nose and then inspected the area closely several times to check that the fall passed through it. I found two loose dominoes beside the line, judged they were off the outline and wouldn't show, and left them alone rather than risk bumping neighbouring work. Once the nose was solid I went hands off so nothing got knocked before the push.

Collaboration: Priya asked me to join her top line into Leo's bottom line, and I told her I'd do it once the nose was round. I then told Maya she could leave that gap, so we didn't double up, and reported back to everyone on the state of the nose. I kept my updates to the manager short and accurate.

Leadership: I took ownership of a specific job without being chased, communicated clearly about what was done and what was left, and made the call to stop building and protect the finished work. I can't claim I shaped the design or steered the table, since that came mainly from Priya and Maya.

Overall, I contributed a small but essential piece: the nose join. I estimate my share of the table's result at about 20 percent.", "my_share_percent": 20}
